svg.title: Five Fee Yields on the Same $100,000 Recovery
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-collectible-base-fee-yield; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Five Fee Yields on the Same $100,000 Recovery; subtitle: Compare earned operator fees, not import value or settlement pool size.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Each independent bar assumes $100,000 of realized eligible client recovery and a stated illustrative contingency within 25%–35%. Bars show revenue before delivery costs, not net profit, expected claim value, or additive annual forecasts. Drawback recovery is calculated after applicable statutory limits, often 99% of qualifying duties, taxes, and fees; $100,000 here is the actual recovery base. Fee terms require client acceptance and must fit the applicable filing arrangement and any settlement-specific restrictions.; caption: Higher headline percentages do not offset weak evidence, delayed cash, duplicate claims, or nonrecoverable duty components.; stages: label: Direct unused-merchandise drawback; value: $25,000 fee at 25%; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Use a substantiated 19 U.S.C. § 1313(j)(1) claim with qualifying unused merchandise and timely export or destruction. Specific identification and clean inventory tracing support the lower illustrative service rate.; label: Substitution drawback; value: $35,000 fee at 35%; numeric value: 35000.0; detail: Use a qualifying 19 U.S.C. § 1313(j)(2) route with the applicable eight-digit HTS classification test, possession requirements, special classification restrictions, and valuation limits. Identical tariff codes alone do not establish eligibility.; label: ACE entry correction refund; value: $25,000 fee at 25%; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Correct an eligible unliquidated entry through ACE Post-Summary Correction using documented classification, valuation, or origin facts. The filing professional verifies current CBP timing rules and entry-type restrictions before preparing the correction.; label: Timely liquidation protest; value: $35,000 fee at 35%; numeric value: 35000.0; detail: Use 19 U.S.C. § 1514 and 19 CFR Part 174 for a protestable decision filed within the applicable deadline. The collectible base is the supported refund actually paid, not the full duties shown on every challenged entry.; label: B2B settlement distribution; value: $30,000 fee at 30%; numeric value: 30000.0; detail: Package eligible purchase or interchange records for an existing court-approved settlement. Apply the fee only to the client's realized distribution under accepted terms, with required filer disclosures and direct-filing information.

text.title: Five Fee Yields on the Same $100,000 Recovery
text.tspan: Five Fee Yields on the Same $100,000 Recovery

circle.title: label: Direct unused-merchandise drawback; value: $25,000 fee at 25%; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Use a substantiated 19 U.S.C. § 1313(j)(1) claim with qualifying unused merchandise and timely export or destruction. Specific identification and clean inventory tracing support the lower illustrative service rate.

label: Substitution drawback; value: $35,000 fee at 35%; numeric value: 35000.0; detail: Use a qualifying 19 U.S.C. § 1313(j)(2) route with the applicable eight-digit HTS classification test, possession requirements, special classification restrictions, and valuation limits. Identical tariff codes alone do not establish eligibility.

label: ACE entry correction refund; value: $25,000 fee at 25%; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Correct an eligible unliquidated entry through ACE Post-Summary Correction using documented classification, valuation, or origin facts. The filing professional verifies current CBP timing rules and entry-type restrictions before preparing the correction.

label: Timely liquidation protest; value: $35,000 fee at 35%; numeric value: 35000.0; detail: Use 19 U.S.C. § 1514 and 19 CFR Part 174 for a protestable decision filed within the applicable deadline. The collectible base is the supported refund actually paid, not the full duties shown on every challenged entry.

label: B2B settlement distribution; value: $30,000 fee at 30%; numeric value: 30000.0; detail: Package eligible purchase or interchange records for an existing court-approved settlement. Apply the fee only to the client's realized distribution under accepted terms, with required filer disclosures and direct-filing information.

text.title: Assumptions: Each independent bar assumes $100,000 of realized eligible client recovery and a stated illustrative contingency within 25%–35%. Bars show revenue before delivery costs, not net profit, expected claim value, or additive annual forecasts. Drawback recovery is calculated after applicable statutory limits, often 99% of qualifying duties, taxes, and fees; $100,000 here is the actual recovery base. Fee terms require client acceptance and must fit the applicable filing arrangement and any settlement-specific restrictions.
